Some intermediate nodes loop back to earlier nodes (creating cycles that handle the non-power-of-two probability), while others lead to terminal outcome nodes. Each transition halves the current probability (multiplying by one-half). A new coin flip is then chosen nondeterministically for the next step.
description.safety_properties: NOT_SPECIFIED
description.liveness_properties: Under fair scheduling, the algorithm eventually reaches a terminal outcome node (one of the six die faces) or the accumulated probability drops below any given positive threshold. This convergence property ensures that the algorithm terminates with probability one.
description.model_bounds: The state space is finite: seven intermediate nodes, six terminal nodes, and two coin flip values. The probability values form an infinite but convergent sequence of dyadic rationals.
description.additional_assumptions: The specification assumes weak fairness on the next-state transition, ensuring the system continues to make progress as long as it has not reached a terminal state. The coin flip is modeled as a nondeterministic choice between two outcomes. The specification relies on a separate module for dyadic rational arithmetic operations (halving and representation).

description.system_overview: This specification models the Knuth-Yao die simulation algorithm as a Markov chain with explicit transition probabilities. Rather than modeling individual coin flips, it directly represents the probabilistic transitions between states, where each transition has probability one-half. The goal is to prove that the process converges to one of six accepting (die face) states.
description.actors_and_components: The system has a single actor: a sequential process that transitions through states of a Markov chain. The chain has seven transient states (starting from an initial state) and six absorbing accepting states corresponding to the six die faces. Probability is tracked as a rational number pair.
description.state_variables: The system tracks two pieces of state: (1) the current node in the Markov chain (one of seven transient states or six accepting states), and (2) the cumulative probability of the current execution path, represented as a rational number (a pair of integers encoding numerator and denominator).
description.initial_state: The system begins in the initial transient state with probability equal to one (represented as a large integer denominator for precision). The initial state has two equally likely successors.
description.actions: The single transition action is a Markov chain step: if the current state is not an accepting state and the normalized probability is nonzero, the system nondeterministically chooses one of the successor states defined in the transition table. Each transition multiplies the current probability by the transition probability (one-half for all transitions in this chain). The transition table defines a binary tree structure with some back-edges, matching the Knuth-Yao construction for simulating a fair die.
description.safety_properties: NOT_SPECIFIED
description.liveness_properties: The specification includes a convergence theorem: under the specification's fairness assumptions, the system eventually either reaches an accepting state (one of the six die faces) or the normalized probability reaches zero.
description.model_bounds: The state space consists of seven transient states and six accepting states. Probability is tracked using integer arithmetic with a fixed precision constant (100000 as the unit probability).
description.additional_assumptions: The specification assumes weak fairness on the next-state transition. Probability arithmetic uses integer pairs with a custom multiplication operator and a normalization function that performs integer division. The precision constant determines the resolution of probability tracking.

description.system_overview: This specification models a trivially simple algorithm that repeatedly increments a counter by two, starting from zero. Its primary purpose is educational: it serves as a beginner exercise for learning formal proof techniques in the TLA+ proof system. The specification includes machine-checked proofs that the counter remains a natural number and that it is always divisible by two.
description.actors_and_components: The system consists of a single sequential process that executes an infinite loop. There are no concurrent actors or distributed components.
description.state_variables: The system tracks a single integer counter representing the accumulated value after successive additions of two.
description.initial_state: The counter starts at zero.
description.actions: There is exactly one action: the counter is incremented by two. This action repeats indefinitely in an infinite loop.
description.safety_properties: Type correctness: the counter is always a natural number (non-negative integer). Evenness: the counter is always evenly divisible by two -- that is, there always exists a natural number that, when multiplied by two, equals the counter value.
description.liveness_properties: NOT_SPECIFIED
description.model_bounds: NOT_SPECIFIED
description.additional_assumptions: The specification is written using PlusCal syntax which is translated to TLA+. The specification includes formal proofs of both the type invariant and the evenness property, structured as hierarchical proof steps with base case, stuttering case, and inductive case.

description.system_overview: This specification models a simple sequential algorithm that finds the largest value in a sequence of natural numbers by scanning from left to right. Its primary purpose is educational: it serves as an exercise in defining and proving type invariants, inductive invariants, and algorithm correctness using the TLA+ proof system.
description.actors_and_components: The system consists of a single sequential process that iterates through a sequence. There are no concurrent actors or distributed components.
description.state_variables: The system tracks: (1) an input sequence of natural numbers that does not change during execution, (2) the current highest value seen so far (initialized to negative one to handle the case of an empty sequence), (3) a loop index tracking the current position in the sequence, and (4) a program counter indicating whether the algorithm is still looping or has finished.
description.initial_state: The input sequence is drawn nondeterministically from the set of all finite sequences of natural numbers. The highest-seen value is negative one. The loop index starts at one (the first position). The program counter indicates the loop has not yet completed.
description.actions: There are two actions: (1) Loop body: if the loop index has not exceeded the length of the sequence, the algorithm compares the element at the current index with the current highest value, keeps whichever is larger, and advances the index by one. If the index exceeds the sequence length, the algorithm transitions to a done state. (2) Termination stuttering: once the algorithm has completed, the system stutters (no state change) to prevent deadlock.
description.safety_properties: Type correctness: the input sequence is always a sequence of natural numbers, the loop index is always between one and the length of the sequence plus one, the loop index is always a natural number, and the highest-seen value is always a natural number or negative one. Inductive invariant: at every point during execution, every element of the sequence at positions before the current loop index is less than or equal to the current highest-seen value. Correctness: after the algorithm terminates, the highest-seen value is greater than or equal to every element in the entire input sequence. When the algorithm finishes, the loop index equals the length of the sequence plus one.
description.liveness_properties: Termination: the algorithm eventually reaches the done state.
description.model_bounds: NOT_SPECIFIED
description.additional_assumptions: The specification is written using PlusCal syntax which is translated to TLA+. The specification includes formal hierarchical proofs of: (1) the type invariant, (2) the inductive invariant (using the type invariant as a lemma), (3) a helper theorem that the loop index equals sequence length plus one upon completion, and (4) overall correctness (derived from the preceding invariants). The max function used returns the first argument when both are equal.

description.system_overview: This specification implements and verifies the lexicographically-least circular substring algorithm from the 1980 paper by Kellogg S. Booth (Information Processing Letters, doi:10.1016/0020-0190(80)90149-0). Given a string viewed as circular (where the end wraps around to the beginning), the algorithm finds the rotation that produces the lexicographically smallest string. The algorithm runs in linear time by building a failure function similar to the one used in the Knuth-Morris-Pratt string matching algorithm.
description.actors_and_components: There are no concurrent actors. The specification models a single sequential algorithm that processes a circular string. The main components are: the input string (a zero-indexed sequence of characters from a finite character set that is a subset of the natural numbers), a failure function array used to track pattern-matching information, and loop control variables that drive the algorithm through its nested loops.
description.state_variables: The system tracks: (1) the input string, a zero-indexed sequence of characters chosen nondeterministically from all possible sequences over the character set (the corpus); (2) the length of the input string; (3) a failure function array indexed from 0 to twice the string length, initialized to a sentinel value meaning undefined; (4) a pattern-match index tracking the current failure function lookup; (5) an outer loop counter running from 1 to just below twice the string length; (6) the current best rotation offset, indicating the start position of the lexicographically smallest rotation found so far; (7) a program counter tracking which labeled step of the algorithm is executing.
description.initial_state: The input string is chosen nondeterministically from all zero-indexed sequences over the character set. The string length is set to the length of the chosen string. The failure function is initialized so every entry maps to the sentinel value. The pattern-match index starts at the sentinel value. The outer loop counter starts at 1. The best rotation offset starts at 0. The program counter starts at the outer loop entry.
description.actions: The algorithm proceeds through labeled steps in a sequential loop structure: (1) Outer loop check: if the loop counter is below twice the string length, continue; otherwise terminate. (2) Failure function lookup: retrieve the failure function value for the current position relative to the best offset. (3) Inner comparison loop: compare the character at the current loop position (modulo string length) with the character at the candidate position (modulo string length). If they differ and the pattern-match index is not the sentinel value, continue the inner loop; otherwise exit to the post-comparison step. (4) If the current character is less than the candidate character during the inner loop, update the best rotation offset. (5) Follow the failure function chain by setting the pattern-match index to its failure function value. (6) Post-comparison: if the characters still differ and the pattern-match index is the sentinel value, check again if the current character is less, and if so update the best offset. Set the failure function entry to the sentinel (resetting it) or to one plus the pattern-match index (extending the match). (7) Increment the loop counter and return to the outer loop check. A stuttering action allows the algorithm to remain in its final state after termination.
description.safety_properties: Type invariant: the input string remains in the corpus, the string length equals the length of the input, the failure function maps to valid indices or the sentinel, the pattern-match index and loop counter are within valid ranges, and the best rotation offset is a valid index of the input string. Correctness: upon termination, the best rotation offset identifies the lexicographically-minimal rotation of the input string -- the rotation at that offset is less than or equal to all other rotations, and among rotations producing the same sequence, it has the smallest shift value.
description.liveness_properties: Termination: the algorithm eventually reaches the terminated state.
description.model_bounds: The character set is a constant that must be a subset of the natural numbers. For model checking, the character set size and maximum string length are configured via a separate model-checking module. The state space grows with both the alphabet size and string length.
description.additional_assumptions: The specification uses zero-indexed sequences (defined in a separate utility module) rather than the standard one-indexed sequences. The circular nature of the string is handled by indexing modulo the string length. The algorithm processes a doubled string (iterating up to twice the string length) to handle the wrap-around without explicit circular indexing logic. The nondeterministic choice of input string means the model checker verifies correctness for all strings over the character set up to the configured maximum length.

description.system_overview: This specification models a binary search algorithm for finding an item in a sorted sequence of integers. It is one of the examples from Section 7.3 of 'Proving Safety Properties' by Leslie Lamport. The module defines the algorithm using PlusCal, provides the translated state-machine specification, and includes a complete machine-checked proof of its partial correctness (safety) property. The algorithm takes a sorted sequence and a target value, and returns either the index of the target in the sequence or zero if the target is not present.
description.actors_and_components: The system is a single sequential algorithm. There is one actor: the search procedure, which iterates over a sorted sequence to locate a target value. No concurrency or multiple processes are involved.
description.state_variables: The system maintains: (1) a sorted sequence of integers drawn from a specified set of integer values, (2) a target value to search for, (3) a lower bound index for the current search range, (4) an upper bound index for the current search range, (5) an output index (zero if the target has not been found, or the position of the target when found), and (6) a program counter tracking whether the algorithm is still running or has terminated.
description.initial_state: The sorted sequence is chosen nondeterministically from the set of all sorted sequences over the specified value set. The target value is chosen nondeterministically from the value set. The lower bound is set to 1 (the start of the sequence). The upper bound is set to the length of the sequence. The output index is set to 0 (not found). The program counter is set to the main loop label.
description.actions: The algorithm has one main action corresponding to one iteration of the binary search loop: (1) If the lower bound does not exceed the upper bound and the output is still zero, compute the midpoint of the current range and retrieve the value at that position. If the midpoint value equals the target, set the output to the midpoint index. If the target is less than the midpoint value, move the upper bound to one below the midpoint. Otherwise, move the lower bound to one above the midpoint. (2) If the loop condition is no longer satisfied (lower bound exceeds upper bound, or a result has been found), the algorithm terminates. A stuttering step is also included to prevent deadlock after termination.
description.safety_properties: Partial correctness: when the algorithm terminates, if the target value exists somewhere in the sorted sequence, then the output index points to a position containing the target value; if the target does not exist in the sequence, the output index is zero. An inductive invariant is defined that strengthens this postcondition to be preserved across all transitions.
description.liveness_properties: Termination: the algorithm eventually reaches its terminal state. This is ensured by weak fairness on the transition relation.
description.model_bounds: The set of allowed integer values is declared as a constant that must be a subset of the integers. For model checking, a companion module redefines the sequence operator to produce only sequences up to a bounded length.
description.additional_assumptions: The set of values is assumed to be a subset of the integers. The sorted sequences are defined as those sequences over the value set where elements are in non-decreasing order. The specification includes a complete machine-checked safety proof using the TLAPS proof system, which verifies that the inductive invariant implies the correctness postcondition.

description.system_overview: This specification models an abstract version of the Quicksort sorting algorithm. It is one of the examples from Section 7.3 of 'Proving Safety Properties' by Leslie Lamport. The module defines the algorithm using PlusCal, provides the translated state-machine specification, and includes a structured proof of its partial correctness property: that if the algorithm terminates, it produces a sorted permutation of the original sequence. The specification abstracts away the partition procedure, instead choosing in a single step an arbitrary result that any valid partition procedure could produce.
description.actors_and_components: The system is a single sequential sorting algorithm. There is one actor: the sort procedure, which repeatedly selects intervals, partitions them, and subdivides the work set until all intervals are singletons. No concurrency is involved.
description.state_variables: The system maintains: (1) the current sequence being sorted, (2) a copy of the original sequence (used for verifying that the final result is a permutation of the input), (3) a set of intervals still to be processed (each interval is a contiguous range of indices), and (4) a program counter tracking whether the algorithm is still running or has terminated.
description.initial_state: The sequence is chosen nondeterministically from all non-empty sequences of integers drawn from the specified value set. The original-sequence copy is set equal to the initial sequence. The work set contains a single interval spanning all indices of the sequence. The program counter is set to the main loop label.
description.actions: The algorithm has one main action corresponding to one iteration of the sorting loop: (1) If the work set is non-empty, select an arbitrary interval from it. If that interval contains exactly one element, simply remove it from the work set. Otherwise, choose a pivot index within the interval, split the interval into a lower subinterval and an upper subinterval around the pivot, nondeterministically choose a new sequence that is a valid partition of the current sequence over the chosen interval and pivot (elements at or below the pivot index are no greater than elements above it, and elements outside the interval are unchanged), update the sequence to this new version, and replace the original interval in the work set with the two new subintervals. (2) If the work set is empty, the algorithm terminates. A stuttering step prevents deadlock after termination.
description.safety_properties: Partial correctness: when the algorithm terminates, the final sequence is a permutation of the original input sequence and is sorted in non-decreasing order. An inductive invariant is defined involving domain partitions, permutation preservation, and relative sortedness between intervals.
description.liveness_properties: Termination: the algorithm eventually reaches its terminal state. This is ensured by weak fairness on the transition relation.
description.model_bounds: The set of allowed integer values is declared as a constant that must be a subset of the integers. For model checking, a companion module redefines the sequence operator to produce only sequences up to a bounded length.
description.additional_assumptions: The set of values is assumed to be a subset of the integers. Permutations are defined via composition with automorphisms of the domain. The partition operator produces all permutations that leave elements outside the interval unchanged while ensuring elements at or below the pivot are no greater than those above it. The specification includes a partial TLAPS-checked proof of the correctness theorem.

description.system_overview: This is a model-checking configuration module for the Boyer-Moore majority vote algorithm. It instantiates the main majority vote specification with concrete parameters to enable exhaustive verification using a model checker: three distinct values and a bounded sequence length.
description.actors_and_components: The module defines three constant model values representing the distinct elements that can appear in sequences, and a bound parameter controlling the maximum sequence length. It instantiates the main majority vote specification with these concrete values.
description.state_variables: The state variables are inherited from the main majority vote specification: the input sequence, the current scan position, the candidate element, and the counter. Additionally, the module defines a bounded sequence operator that restricts sequences to those of length at most the specified bound.
description.initial_state: Inherited from the main specification: sequences are drawn from all sequences of up to the bounded length over the three-element value set, the scan position starts at one, the candidate is chosen nondeterministically, and the counter starts at zero.
description.actions: All actions are inherited from the main majority vote specification: scanning the next element with the three-case logic (adopt new candidate, increment counter, or decrement counter).
description.safety_properties: Inherited from the main specification: type correctness, the main correctness property (any true majority element must equal the candidate after a complete scan), and the inductive invariant.
description.liveness_properties: Inherited from the main specification: the scan eventually completes under weak fairness.
description.model_bounds: Three model values for the element set. The sequence length bound is set to 5 in the configuration. Sequences are restricted to all functions from one through n to the value set, for n ranging from zero to the bound.
description.additional_assumptions: The bound parameter is assumed to be a natural number. The module uses a bounded sequence construction rather than the standard sequence definition to keep the state space finite for model checking. Deadlock checking is disabled in the configuration.

description.system_overview: This module contains an interactive formal proof of correctness for the Boyer-Moore majority vote algorithm. It extends the main algorithm specification with lemmas and a machine-checked proof that the algorithm correctly identifies the only possible majority element. The proof is structured to be verified by the TLA+ Proof System (TLAPS).
description.actors_and_components: The module imports the main majority vote specification and extends it with proof obligations. It uses finite set theory lemmas from a standard proof library. The proof establishes two main results: type correctness and the correctness of the algorithm's output.
description.state_variables: No new state variables are introduced. All state variables are inherited from the main majority vote specification.
description.initial_state: Inherited from the main specification.
description.actions: No new actions are defined. All transitions are inherited from the main specification.
description.safety_properties: Two properties are formally proved: (1) Type correctness is an invariant of the specification, proved by showing it holds initially and is preserved by every transition. (2) The main correctness property is an invariant: after scanning the entire sequence, any value occurring in a strict majority of positions must equal the candidate. This is proved via the inductive invariant from the main specification.
description.liveness_properties: NOT_SPECIFIED
description.model_bounds: NOT_SPECIFIED
description.additional_assumptions: The proof relies on TLAPS (TLA+ Proof System) for machine-checked verification. It uses auxiliary lemmas about finite set cardinality and properties of occurrence counting functions (positions before a given index form finite subsets of integers, adding an element to a finite set increases cardinality by one, etc.). The proof structure is hierarchical with numbered proof steps.

description.system_overview: This specification models the Boyer-Moore majority vote algorithm, an efficient single-pass algorithm that identifies the only candidate element in a sequence that could hold a strict majority (appearing in more than half the positions). The algorithm was originally published by R.S. Boyer and J.S. Moore in a 1981 technical report and later in print in 1991. It uses constant extra space beyond the input sequence.
description.actors_and_components: The system has a single sequential actor that scans through an input sequence of values from a finite nonempty set. There are no concurrent processes or distributed components.
description.state_variables: The system tracks four pieces of state: (1) the input sequence of values, which is chosen nondeterministically at initialization and never modified, (2) a position index indicating the next element to examine, (3) the current candidate for majority element, and (4) a counter representing a lower bound on how many more times the candidate has appeared compared to other elements in the portion scanned so far.
description.initial_state: The input sequence is chosen nondeterministically from all possible sequences over the value set. The position index starts at the first position. The candidate is chosen nondeterministically from the value set. The counter starts at zero.
description.actions: There is one transition that executes when the position index has not yet passed the end of the sequence. Three cases arise: (1) If the counter is zero, the current element becomes the new candidate and the counter is set to one. (2) If the counter is nonzero and the current element matches the candidate, the counter is incremented. (3) If the counter is nonzero and the current element differs from the candidate, the counter is decremented. In all cases, the position index advances by one and the input sequence remains unchanged.
description.safety_properties: The main correctness property is: once the scan is complete (the position index exceeds the sequence length), if any value occurs in a strict majority of positions in the sequence, then that value must equal the current candidate. An inductive invariant supports this: (a) the counter never exceeds the number of times the candidate has appeared so far, (b) twice the excess occurrences of the candidate beyond the counter does not exceed the number of non-candidate positions scanned, and (c) for every non-candidate value, twice its occurrence count does not exceed the number of non-candidate positions scanned. A type correctness invariant ensures all variables remain in their expected domains.
description.liveness_properties: Under weak fairness, the algorithm eventually completes its scan of the entire sequence (the position index eventually exceeds the sequence length).
description.model_bounds: The value set and sequence length bounds are provided as model-checking parameters. A companion model-checking module defines a set of three distinct values and bounds the sequence length.
description.additional_assumptions: The specification assumes the value set is nonempty. Weak fairness is assumed on the next-state action. The input sequence is modeled as a variable (rather than a constant) to allow the model checker to verify the algorithm for all sequences up to a bounded size.

description.system_overview: A multiprocess parallel implementation of Misra's graph reachability algorithm. Multiple processes concurrently explore a directed graph to compute the set of nodes reachable from a given root node. Each process independently picks frontier nodes, marks them, and adds their successors to the shared frontier one at a time. The module proves that this parallel algorithm implements (refines) the sequential Misra algorithm under a defined refinement mapping.
description.actors_and_components: A finite set of worker processes that execute concurrently. Each process has local variables tracking its currently selected node and its local set of successors still to be added to the shared frontier. All processes share a global set of marked nodes and a global frontier set. Written in PlusCal with the attached translation.
description.state_variables: Five state variables: (1) the shared set of marked (visited) nodes, (2) the shared frontier set of nodes to explore, (3) per-process program counters indicating each process's current execution point, (4) per-process local variable holding the node currently being processed, and (5) per-process local set of successor nodes that still need to be added to the frontier.
description.initial_state: The marked set is empty. The frontier contains only the root node. Each process starts at the beginning of its main loop with its local node set to the root and its local successor set empty.
description.actions: Three per-process actions at distinct control points. (1) At the loop head: if the frontier is non-empty, pick an arbitrary frontier node and store it locally; if the frontier is empty, the process terminates. (2) At the marking step: if the local node is not yet marked, add it to marked and set the local successor set to all its graph successors; otherwise, remove the local node from the frontier and return to the loop head. (3) At the successor-adding step: if the local successor set is non-empty, pick one node from it, add it to the frontier, and remove it from the local set; when all successors have been added, return to the loop head.
description.safety_properties: The parallel algorithm refines the sequential Misra algorithm. An inductive invariant establishes type correctness and two key relationships: each process's local successor set is empty except when the process is in the successor-adding phase, and a process's selected node is in the frontier or marked set when the process is at the marking step. The refinement mapping defines the sequential algorithm's frontier as the parallel frontier plus all processes' local successor sets, and the sequential program counter as terminated only when all parallel processes have terminated.
description.liveness_properties: The algorithm terminates if and only if the set of reachable nodes is finite. When it terminates, the marked set equals exactly the set of nodes reachable from the root. Weak fairness is assumed for each process.
description.model_bounds: NOT_SPECIFIED
description.additional_assumptions: The root is a valid graph node. The process set is non-empty and finite. A process may observe the frontier as empty and terminate before all reachable nodes are found, but correctness is maintained because at least one process will continue running until the computation is complete. In practice, the frontier emptiness test can be implemented to reduce premature termination.

description.system_overview: A specification of Misra's algorithm for computing the set of nodes reachable from a given root node in a directed graph. The algorithm is a variant of breadth-first search that differs from the standard algorithm in that the set of visited nodes and the frontier set may overlap, making it amenable to parallel implementation. Written in PlusCal with an attached translation.
description.actors_and_components: A single sequential process that explores the graph. It maintains a set of visited (marked) nodes and a frontier set of nodes yet to be fully explored. The algorithm picks nodes from the frontier and either marks them and adds their successors to the frontier, or removes them if already marked.
description.state_variables: Three state variables: (1) the set of nodes that have been marked (visited), (2) the frontier set of nodes to explore (which may overlap with marked nodes, unlike standard breadth-first search), and (3) a program counter tracking whether the algorithm is running or has terminated.
description.initial_state: The marked set is empty. The frontier contains only the root node. The program counter indicates the algorithm is at the start of its main loop.
description.actions: One main action with two cases, chosen nondeterministically from the frontier. If the chosen node is not yet marked: add it to the marked set and add all its successors to the frontier (without removing the node from the frontier). If the chosen node is already marked: remove it from the frontier. The algorithm terminates when the frontier is empty.
description.safety_properties: Partial correctness: when the algorithm terminates, the marked set equals exactly the set of nodes reachable from the root. This is established through three invariants: (1) every successor of a marked node is in the marked set or the frontier, (2) the union of the marked set and the nodes reachable from the frontier equals the nodes reachable from the union of marked and frontier, (3) the set of nodes reachable from the root equals the marked set plus nodes reachable from the frontier. A type correctness invariant ensures both sets contain only valid graph nodes.
description.liveness_properties: If the set of reachable nodes is finite, the algorithm eventually terminates. This follows from weak fairness of the main action: the frontier cannot remain non-empty forever because each cycle of the loop either adds a new element to the finite marked set or removes an element from the frontier.
description.model_bounds: NOT_SPECIFIED
description.additional_assumptions: The root is assumed to be a valid node in the graph. The algorithm works correctly for both finite and infinite graphs, but termination is guaranteed only when the reachable set is finite. The key insight of Misra's variant is that allowing overlap between marked and frontier nodes simplifies parallelization, as described in the companion parallel implementation module.

description.system_overview: A model of the classic missionaries and cannibals river-crossing puzzle. Three missionaries and three cannibals must cross a river using a boat that carries at most two people. On either bank, if missionaries are present, they must not be outnumbered by cannibals (otherwise the cannibals would eat them). The boat cannot cross the river empty. The goal is to find a sequence of moves that transports everyone safely from one bank to the other.
actors_and_components: Missionaries: A set of three people who must cross the river without being outnumbered by cannibals on either bank.
Cannibals: A set of three people who must also cross the river. If they outnumber missionaries on a bank where missionaries are present, the missionaries are eaten.
Boat: A vessel that carries one or two people across the river per trip. It cannot travel empty.
state_variables: Which bank the boat is currently docked at (east or west).
A mapping from each bank to the set of people (missionaries and cannibals) currently on that bank.
description.initial_state: The boat is docked at the east bank. All missionaries and all cannibals are on the east bank. The west bank is empty.
actions: Move: A group of one or two people boards the boat on the current bank and crosses to the opposite bank. This action is only enabled when the resulting configuration on both banks is safe (no missionaries are outnumbered by cannibals on either bank). After the move, the boat is docked at the destination bank, and the people distribution is updated accordingly.
safety_properties: On every bank, if any missionaries are present, cannibals must not outnumber them. Equivalently, either a bank has no missionaries, or the count of cannibals on that bank is less than or equal to the count of missionaries.
The boat carries exactly one or two people per crossing (never zero, never more than two).
description.liveness_properties: NOT_SPECIFIED
additional_assumptions: The puzzle is solved when the east bank becomes empty (everyone has reached the west bank). The specification is designed so that a model checker finding a violation of the 'east bank is non-empty' invariant produces a solution trace.
A bank is considered safe if it contains only cannibals (no missionaries to endanger) or if the number of cannibals does not exceed the number of missionaries.

description.system_overview: This specification models a multi-car elevator system in a building with multiple floors. Multiple elevators service requests from people who wish to travel between floors. The specification includes a simple dispatch algorithm that selects the closest available elevator to service each call, and temporal properties ensure that every call is eventually serviced and every waiting person eventually reaches their destination.
description.actors_and_components: The system has three types of actors: (1) People, who decide on destination floors, call elevators, enter and exit elevators. (2) Elevators, which move between floors, open and close doors, and carry people. (3) A dispatcher that assigns elevators to service floor calls based on proximity. Each person has a location (either a floor or inside an elevator), a destination floor, and a waiting status. Each elevator has a current floor, a direction of travel (up, down, or stationary), a door state (open or closed), and a set of floor buttons that have been pressed by passengers inside.
description.state_variables: The system tracks: (1) the state of each person, including their current location (a floor number or an elevator identifier), their desired destination floor, and whether they are currently waiting for an elevator; (2) a set of active elevator calls, where each call specifies a floor and a direction; (3) the state of each elevator, including its current floor, its direction of movement (up, down, or stationary), whether its doors are open, and the set of floor buttons pressed by its passengers.
description.initial_state: All people start on arbitrary floors with arbitrary destination floors. No person is waiting. There are no active elevator calls. All elevators start on arbitrary floors, stationary, with doors closed and no buttons pressed.
description.actions: The following actions can occur: (1) Pick new destination: a person who is not waiting and is on a floor chooses a new destination floor different from their current floor. (2) Call elevator: a person who is not waiting and whose destination differs from their location begins waiting and creates an elevator call for their floor and intended direction, unless an elevator is already at their floor going the right direction with doors open. (3) Open elevator doors: an elevator opens its doors if it is at a floor with a matching active call or a pressed button for that floor, clearing the corresponding call and button. (4) Enter elevator: all people waiting on the elevator's floor who are traveling in the elevator's direction enter the elevator, and their destination floor buttons are pressed. (5) Exit elevator: all passengers whose destination is the elevator's current floor exit onto that floor and stop waiting. (6) Close elevator doors: the elevator closes its doors once no one can enter or exit at the current floor. (7) Move elevator: the elevator moves one floor in its current direction, provided its doors are closed, it does not need to stop at the current floor, and any active call it could service is also coverable by another elevator. (8) Stop elevator: the elevator becomes stationary when it reaches the boundary floor and cannot continue in its current direction. (9) Dispatch elevator: when a call is active, the system selects the closest elevator that is either stationary or already approaching the call floor in the same direction, and directs it toward the call; a stationary elevator jumps directly to the call floor.
description.safety_properties: Type invariant: person states, elevator calls, and elevator states all conform to their expected types. Safety invariant: (1) an elevator has a floor button pressed only if some person inside that elevator is going to that floor; (2) if a person is inside a moving elevator, the elevator is moving toward that person's destination; (3) there are no ghost calls -- every active call has at least one person actually waiting at that floor for that direction.
description.liveness_properties: Every elevator call is eventually serviced by some elevator arriving at the call floor moving in the requested direction. Every person who is waiting for an elevator eventually arrives at their destination floor.
description.model_bounds: The set of people, the set of elevators, and the number of floors are declared as constants. Typical small model-checking configurations use 2 people, 2 elevators, and 2 floors. Medium configurations might use more people or floors.
description.additional_assumptions: Weak fairness is assumed for calling elevators, opening doors, entering elevators, exiting elevators, and stopping elevators. Strong fairness is assumed for closing doors, moving elevators, and dispatching elevators. The dispatch algorithm is simple and does not optimize for global throughput or average wait time -- it merely picks the closest eligible elevator. People may nondeterministically choose new destination floors at any time when not waiting.

description.system_overview: A practical state machine replication (SMR) style specification of the MultiPaxos consensus protocol for strongly-consistent replication of a log of commands. Unlike abstract Paxos specifications, this model closely mirrors how a real distributed key-value store would implement MultiPaxos, with explicit server replicas maintaining logs of command instances, clients issuing write and read commands, and a leader election mechanism based on ballot numbers.
description.actors_and_components: Three types of actors: (1) server replicas that participate in consensus, maintain local logs, and may act as leaders or followers; (2) clients represented implicitly through a sequence of pending write and read commands; and (3) an asynchronous network modeled as a monotonically growing set of sent messages (messages may be delayed, duplicated, or effectively lost but retried). Written in PlusCal with the attached translation.
description.state_variables: Four global state variables: (1) the set of messages that have been sent on the network, (2) per-replica node state including leader identity, current key value, commit progress, ballot numbers (prepared and maximum known), and a log of instance states (each tracking status, command, and voted ballot/command), (3) a sequence of pending client commands not yet processed, and (4) a sequence of observed client events recording the order of request and acknowledgement events.
description.initial_state: The network is empty. Every replica starts with no leader, a nil key value, zero commit progress, zero ballot numbers, and all log slots empty. The pending commands sequence contains all write commands followed by all read commands. The observed events sequence is empty.
description.actions: Seven actions per replica, executed in a nondeterministic loop until termination. (1) Become leader: a non-leader picks a fresh higher ballot, resets its preparation state, and broadcasts a prepare message. (2) Handle prepare: a follower receiving a prepare with a higher ballot updates its known ballot and replies with its voted log entries. (3) Handle prepare replies: a leader waiting for preparation collects a majority of replies, marks its ballot as prepared, and adopts the highest-voted commands for each slot. (4) Take new request: a prepared leader picks the next pending command, assigns it to the first empty slot, broadcasts an accept message, and records the request event. (5) Handle accept: a replica receiving an accept with a valid ballot updates its log slot and replies. (6) Handle accept replies: a leader collecting a majority of accept replies commits the slot, applies the command to its key-value state, records the acknowledgement event, and broadcasts a commit notice. (7) Handle commit notice: a follower receiving a commit notice marks the corresponding slot as committed and applies the command.
description.safety_properties: NOT_SPECIFIED
description.liveness_properties: Semi-liveness is checked by requiring no deadlocks until all commands have been processed, requested, and acknowledged. An explicit termination condition requires that all pending commands are consumed and all request/acknowledgement events are observed.
description.model_bounds: NOT_SPECIFIED
description.additional_assumptions: Several optimizations reduce the state space without loss of generality: ballot numbers from different proposers are unique, commands are picked in a fixed order, and each command appears at most once in a prepared log. The pending command sequence is fixed (writes before reads) since other orderings are symmetric or less interesting. The specification supports extension with features like node failure injection and leader leases.

description.system_overview: This specification models the N-Queens problem using PlusCal, an algorithmic language that translates to TLA+. It implements the same iterative backtracking algorithm as the plain TLA+ version: given an N-by-N chessboard, find all arrangements of N queens such that no two queens threaten each other (no shared row, column, or diagonal). The PlusCal version makes the sequential control flow explicit through a labeled while loop.
description.actors_and_components: The system consists of a single solver that iteratively processes partial queen placements. The solver uses a loop that repeatedly selects a partial placement, computes all valid single-row extensions, and either records complete solutions or queues new partial placements for further processing.
description.state_variables: The system tracks three pieces of state: (1) a set of partial placements awaiting processing, where each partial placement is an ordered list of column positions shorter than the board size, (2) a set of completed solutions found so far, where each is a complete list of column positions of length N, and (3) a program counter that tracks whether the algorithm is still iterating or has finished.
description.initial_state: The work set contains a single empty placement (no queens placed). The result set is empty. The program counter indicates the algorithm is at the beginning of its main loop.
description.actions: While the work set is non-empty, the solver selects any partial placement, determines the next row to fill, and computes all columns where a new queen can be placed without conflicting with previously placed queens. A conflict means two queens share the same column or the same diagonal. Each valid extension is constructed by appending the chosen column to the partial placement. If this completes all N rows, the extension goes into the result set; otherwise it goes into the work set. The selected partial placement is removed from the work set. When the work set is empty, the algorithm transitions to a done state and permits only stuttering steps.
description.safety_properties: The result set contains only valid solutions: no completed placement has two queens that attack each other. When the algorithm terminates, the result set contains every possible valid placement.
description.liveness_properties: The algorithm eventually terminates: the program counter eventually reaches the done state, meaning all partial placements have been fully explored.
description.model_bounds: The board size N is a constant positive natural number. For model checking, N must be set to a specific finite value.
description.additional_assumptions: The PlusCal translation includes an explicit termination-detecting step that allows infinite stuttering once the algorithm completes, preventing the model checker from reporting deadlock. A separate liveness condition can be added via weak fairness on the main loop action to guarantee termination.

description.system_overview: This specification models the N-Queens problem, a classic combinatorial puzzle that asks how to place N chess queens on an N-by-N chessboard such that no two queens threaten each other. The specification defines what constitutes a valid solution and provides an iterative algorithm that systematically constructs all solutions by extending partial placements one row at a time.
description.actors_and_components: The system consists of a single solver process that maintains a work set of partial queen placements and a result set of completed solutions. Each placement assigns one queen per row, recording which column that queen occupies. The solver repeatedly picks a partial placement, attempts to extend it by one row, and either produces a complete solution or generates new partial placements for further extension.
description.state_variables: The system tracks two collections: (1) a set of partial placements still to be processed, where each partial placement is an ordered list of column positions shorter than the board size, and (2) a set of completed solutions found so far, where each solution is an ordered list of column positions of length equal to the board size.
description.initial_state: The work set contains a single empty placement (no queens placed yet). The result set is empty (no solutions found).
description.actions: The solver selects any partial placement from the work set, determines which row to fill next, and computes all columns where a queen can be placed without conflicting with any previously placed queen. A conflict occurs when two queens share the same column or lie on the same diagonal. For each valid column, the solver creates an extended placement. If the extended placement covers all rows, it is added to the result set; otherwise, it is added to the work set. The original partial placement is removed from the work set.
description.safety_properties: The result set contains only valid solutions at all times: every completed placement in the result set has no two queens attacking each other. When the work set becomes empty, the result set contains all possible solutions.
description.liveness_properties: The work set eventually becomes empty, meaning the algorithm terminates and all solutions have been found.
description.model_bounds: The board size N is a constant positive natural number. For model checking, N must be instantiated with a specific finite value (typically small values like 4 or 5, since the state space grows rapidly).
description.additional_assumptions: Weak fairness is assumed on the solver's extension action, ensuring the algorithm continues making progress as long as there are partial placements remaining. The board size must be at least 1.

description.system_overview: This specification models the abstract consensus problem, in which a set of processes must cooperatively choose a single value from a set of proposed values. It captures the most fundamental safety requirement of consensus: that at most one value is ever chosen. The specification abstracts away individual processes entirely and focuses only on the set of chosen values.
description.actors_and_components: There are no explicit process identities or roles in this specification. The system is modeled purely in terms of the set of values that can be proposed and the set of values that have been chosen. The set of proposable values is a declared constant.
description.state_variables: The system tracks a single piece of state: the set of values that have been chosen so far.
description.initial_state: Initially, no value has been chosen. The set of chosen values is empty.
description.actions: There is exactly one kind of transition: if no value has been chosen yet, the system may select any single value from the set of proposable values and record it as the chosen value. Once a value is chosen, no further transitions are enabled -- the system reaches a terminal state.
description.safety_properties: The chosen set is always a subset of the declared value set, and the number of chosen values never exceeds one. In other words, at most one value is ever chosen, and once chosen it cannot be revoked or changed. This is expressed as an invariant that the cardinality of the chosen set is at most one and all elements are valid values.
description.liveness_properties: Under a weak fairness assumption on the choosing action, a value is eventually chosen. Without that fairness assumption, the base specification permits the system to stutter forever without choosing any value.
description.model_bounds: The set of proposable values is a finite constant. For model checking, it is typically instantiated with a small set (for example, three model values).
description.additional_assumptions: The specification includes a machine-checked proof that the safety invariant (at most one value chosen) holds. The proof uses standard finite-set cardinality reasoning. The specification also extends standard arithmetic and finite-set library modules, and uses a proof-system backend for formal verification.

description.system_overview: This is a model-checking configuration module for verifying the abstract consensus specification. It reformulates the inductive invariant of the consensus specification so that it can serve as an initial predicate for TLC, enabling TLC to check that the invariant is preserved by every step of the specification.
description.actors_and_components: Same as the base consensus specification: no explicit processes, just the set of proposable values and the chosen set. This module extends the base consensus specification.
description.state_variables: Same as the base consensus specification: the set of chosen values. The type invariant is restated so that the chosen set is declared as an element of the power set of the value set (required for TLC to use it as an initial predicate).
description.initial_state: The initial state for inductive invariant checking is the invariant itself (not the original empty-set initial state). This allows TLC to explore all states satisfying the invariant and verify that every successor state also satisfies it.
description.actions: Same as the base consensus specification: the single transition that selects a value when no value has yet been chosen.
description.safety_properties: The inductive invariant asserts that the chosen set is a subset of the value set and has cardinality at most one. This module provides a specification whose initial states are all states satisfying the invariant, enabling TLC to verify inductiveness.
description.liveness_properties: NOT_SPECIFIED
description.model_bounds: The set of proposable values is instantiated with a finite set. For model checking, the value set is typically small (for example, three model values).
description.additional_assumptions: This module is a companion to the base consensus specification and relies on the definitions and operators from that specification. It is used specifically for model-checking the inductive invariant with TLC.

description.system_overview: This is a model-checking configuration module for verifying the Paxos consensus algorithm specification. It provides finite instantiations of the constants, definitions for checking the inductive invariant, and support for verifying that the Paxos algorithm implements the abstract voting specification. It also includes a liveness specification for checking progress.
description.actors_and_components: The module declares three model acceptors and two model values. Quorums are defined as the three possible majority subsets of the three acceptors. The module extends the base Paxos specification and provides definitions needed for TLC model checking.
description.state_variables: Same as the base Paxos specification: per-acceptor participation threshold, per-acceptor highest vote ballot, per-acceptor highest vote value, and the message set. The type invariant is reformulated so that the message set is declared using set membership (element of power set) rather than subset notation, as required for TLC initial predicates.
description.initial_state: For standard model checking, the initial state comes from the base Paxos specification. For inductive invariant checking, the initial state is the reformulated invariant itself, allowing TLC to explore all invariant-satisfying states.
description.actions: Same as the base Paxos specification: Phase 1a (prepare), Phase 1b (promise), Phase 2a (accept-request), and Phase 2b (acceptance). For liveness checking, weak fairness conditions are applied to Phase 1a for the maximum ballot, Phase 2a for the maximum ballot with every value, and Phase 1b and Phase 2b for specific acceptors.
description.safety_properties: The inductive invariant is decomposed into four separate conjuncts for easier debugging: (1) type correctness, (2) consistency between per-acceptor vote tracking and the derived vote set, (3) constraints on message contents including that promise messages reflect actual votes and accept-request messages are justified by quorum safety, and (4) the invariant of the abstract voting specification. Additionally, the module checks that the refinement mapping to the voting specification is preserved.
description.liveness_properties: Under the fairness conditions, eventually some value is chosen (the derived chosen set in the voting specification becomes non-empty).
description.model_bounds: Three acceptors, two values, quorums are all majority subsets, and a configurable maximum ballot number that bounds the ballot range to zero through that maximum. Symmetry is exploited over the acceptor and value sets.
description.additional_assumptions: This module is a companion to the base Paxos specification. Multiple specifications are provided for different checking modes: standard specification checking, inductive invariant checking, and liveness checking. The module also defines a property asserting that every step preserves the voting specification's next-state relation under the refinement mapping.

description.system_overview: This is a model-checking configuration module for verifying the abstract voting-based consensus specification. It provides finite instantiations of the constants, several alternative specifications for checking different properties, and definitions to verify that the voting algorithm implements the abstract consensus specification.
description.actors_and_components: The module declares three model acceptors and two model values. Quorums are defined as the three possible majority subsets of the three acceptors. The module extends the base voting specification.
description.state_variables: Same as the base voting specification: per-acceptor vote sets and per-acceptor promise thresholds.
description.initial_state: For standard specification checking, the initial state comes from the base voting specification. For theorem checking, the initial state is the type invariant (all type-correct states), used to verify theorems about safety concepts. For inductive invariant checking, the initial state is the full invariant.
description.actions: Same as the base voting specification: increasing an acceptor's promise threshold and casting a vote for a value in a ballot. An alternative specification using a false next-state relation (no steps allowed) is provided for checking that certain properties hold in all type-correct states without any transitions.
description.safety_properties: The module checks: (1) the main invariant (type correctness, vote safety, and one value per ballot), (2) several theorems including that all values are safe at ballot zero, the choosability theorem, the one-vote-per-ballot theorem, the votes-safe-implies-consistency theorem, and the shows-safety theorem, (3) that the voting specification implements the abstract consensus specification via a refinement property.
description.liveness_properties: NOT_SPECIFIED
description.model_bounds: Three acceptors, two values, quorums are all majority subsets, and ballot numbers bounded to zero through one (or zero through two). Symmetry is exploited over the acceptor and value sets. Deadlock checking is disabled.
description.additional_assumptions: This module is a companion to the base voting specification. It includes an assumption check that quorums are non-empty. Multiple specifications are provided for different verification modes: standard behavior checking, static theorem checking over type-correct states, and inductive invariant checking.

description.system_overview: This specification models the Paxos consensus algorithm, a message-passing protocol that allows a set of processes to agree on a single value despite potential failures. It is a refinement of the abstract voting-based consensus specification, adding explicit message passing between leaders (proposers) and acceptors. The algorithm proceeds in numbered ballots, each with a designated leader, and ensures that at most one value is ever chosen.
description.actors_and_components: The system has three types of participants: (1) Leaders -- one per ballot number, responsible for orchestrating the two-phase protocol for that ballot. In practice, a finite number of leader processes each play the leader role for infinitely many ballot numbers. (2) Acceptors -- processes that receive messages and cast votes. (3) Quorums -- sets of acceptors, where any two quorums must overlap. Learner processes that discover chosen values are omitted from this specification.
description.state_variables: The system tracks four pieces of state: (1) For each acceptor, the highest ballot number in which it has participated or promised to participate (initialized to negative one). (2) For each acceptor, the ballot number of the highest-numbered ballot in which it has cast a vote (initialized to negative one). (3) For each acceptor, the value it voted for in that highest ballot (initialized to a distinguished 'no value' sentinel). (4) The set of all messages that have been sent. Messages are added to this set but never removed, modeling an asynchronous network.
description.initial_state: All acceptor participation thresholds and vote-ballot trackers are set to negative one. All acceptor vote-value trackers are set to the 'no value' sentinel. The message set is empty.
description.actions: The protocol has four actions: (1) Phase 1a: A leader initiates a ballot by broadcasting a prepare message containing the ballot number. (2) Phase 1b: An acceptor that receives a prepare message with a ballot number higher than any it has seen updates its participation threshold and replies with a promise message containing the ballot number of its most recent vote and the value it voted for (or negative one and the sentinel if it has never voted). (3) Phase 2a: Once a leader has collected promise replies from a quorum for its ballot, it selects a value to propose. If any responder had previously voted, the leader must choose the value from the response with the highest previous ballot number. If no responder had voted, the leader is free to propose any value. The leader then broadcasts an accept-request message with the ballot number and the selected value. At most one accept-request may be sent per ballot. (4) Phase 2b: An acceptor that receives an accept-request for a ballot number at least as high as its current threshold accepts the proposal by updating its vote tracker to record the ballot number and value, and broadcasts an acceptance message.
description.safety_properties: Consistency: at most one value is ever chosen. A value is chosen when a quorum of acceptors have all accepted the same value in the same ballot. The specification maintains an inductive invariant ensuring that the algorithm implements the abstract voting protocol, which in turn implements abstract consensus. Type correctness of all variables and messages is also maintained as an invariant.
description.liveness_properties: NOT_SPECIFIED
description.model_bounds: Ballot numbers are natural numbers, bounded to a finite range for model checking. The sets of acceptors, values, and quorums are declared as constants. The message type set includes four kinds of messages: prepare, promise, accept-request, and acceptance.
description.additional_assumptions: Any two quorums must have a non-empty intersection. Messages are never removed from the message pool, modeling an asynchronous network where messages may be duplicated or arbitrarily delayed. There is no need to model message loss explicitly because the safety specification only constrains what may happen, not what must happen. The specification instantiates the voting algorithm module and defines a refinement mapping showing that the Paxos algorithm implements the voting specification. A distinguished value that is not in the ballot set is used as a sentinel for acceptors that have not yet voted.

description.system_overview: This specification models a high-level voting-based consensus algorithm in which a set of acceptor processes cooperatively choose a single value. It is a high-level abstraction of the Paxos consensus algorithm that abstracts away the details of message passing. The algorithm ensures that once a value is chosen (by receiving votes from a quorum of acceptors in the same ballot), no different value can ever be chosen.
description.actors_and_components: The system has three types of participants: (1) Acceptors -- processes that cast votes for values in numbered ballots. (2) Quorums -- sets of acceptors, where any two quorums must share at least one acceptor. (3) Values -- the set of values that can be proposed and chosen. There are no explicit proposer or leader roles; the algorithm focuses on how acceptors cast votes.
description.state_variables: The system tracks two pieces of state per acceptor: (1) the set of votes that each acceptor has cast, where each vote is a pair of a ballot number and a value; and (2) a promise threshold for each acceptor, indicating the minimum ballot number in which the acceptor will participate going forward (initialized to negative one, meaning no promise has been made).
description.initial_state: Initially, no acceptor has cast any votes (each acceptor's vote set is empty) and no acceptor has made any promise (each acceptor's threshold is negative one).
description.actions: There are two types of transitions: (1) An acceptor may increase its promise threshold to any higher ballot number without casting a vote. This prevents the acceptor from voting in any ballot below the new threshold. (2) An acceptor may vote for a value in a ballot, subject to four conditions: the ballot number must not be below the acceptor's current threshold; the acceptor must not have already voted in that ballot; no other acceptor may have voted for a different value in that same ballot; and there must exist a quorum demonstrating that the value is safe at that ballot number. Casting a vote also updates the acceptor's threshold to the ballot number. A value is safe at ballot number b if, for every lower ballot c, there exists a quorum in which every member has either voted for that value in ballot c or can never vote in ballot c.
description.safety_properties: Consistency: the set of chosen values contains at most one value. That is, if a quorum of acceptors have all voted for the same value in some ballot, and a quorum have all voted for some value in another ballot, those values must be the same. This follows from three invariants: (a) every vote cast is safe at its ballot number, (b) at most one value is voted for per ballot across all acceptors, and (c) the type correctness of votes and thresholds.
description.liveness_properties: NOT_SPECIFIED
description.model_bounds: The set of ballot numbers is the natural numbers. For model checking, ballot numbers are bounded to a finite range (for example, zero through one or zero through two). The sets of acceptors, values, and quorums are declared as constants and instantiated with small finite sets for model checking.
description.additional_assumptions: The specification assumes that quorums satisfy the overlap property: any two quorums have a non-empty intersection. This is essential for the consistency guarantee. Ballot numbers are natural numbers. The specification includes a proof outline showing that the invariant is preserved, and it instantiates the abstract consensus specification to prove that the voting algorithm implements consensus via a refinement mapping where the chosen set is derived from the votes. The specification includes formal proofs checked by a proof system backend.

description.system_overview: This specification models the abstract consensus problem, where a set of processes must choose a single value. It captures the simplest possible formalization: initially no value is chosen, a single value may be selected from a set of candidates, and after that the chosen set never changes. This specification is intended as a tutorial example accompanying a presentation on the Paxos algorithm.
description.actors_and_components: There are no explicit processes or roles. The specification abstracts away all participants and models only the observable outcome: which values have been chosen. The set of candidate values is a declared constant.
description.state_variables: The system tracks a single piece of state: the set of values that have been chosen.
description.initial_state: Initially, no value has been chosen. The chosen set is empty.
description.actions: There is one transition: if the chosen set is currently empty, the system may pick any single value from the candidate set and set the chosen set to contain exactly that value. Once a value is chosen, no further transitions are enabled and the system halts.
description.safety_properties: The chosen set is always a subset of the candidate value set, and the cardinality of the chosen set never exceeds one. Equivalently, at most one value is ever chosen, and a chosen value can never be revoked.
description.liveness_properties: NOT_SPECIFIED
description.model_bounds: The candidate value set is typically instantiated with three model values (for example, a, b, c) for TLC model checking. Deadlock checking is disabled because the system intentionally terminates after choosing a value.
description.additional_assumptions: The specification includes a machine-checked proof of the safety invariant using a proof system backend. The proof uses finite-set cardinality lemmas. The specification extends standard arithmetic, finite-set, and proof-system library modules. This module is designed to be instantiated by higher-level specifications (such as the voting algorithm) that implement consensus through a refinement mapping.

description.system_overview: This specification models the Paxos consensus algorithm with explicit message passing. It refines the abstract voting specification by introducing leaders and acceptors that communicate through four types of messages. The algorithm ensures that at most one value is ever chosen, even in the presence of message delays and process failures. This specification was presented as part of a Turing Award lecture on Paxos.
description.actors_and_components: The system has leaders (one per ballot number, responsible for driving the two-phase protocol), acceptors (processes that respond to leader messages and cast votes), and quorums (sets of acceptors with the property that any two quorums overlap). Learner processes that discover chosen values are omitted. In practice, a finite number of leader processes each play the leader role for many ballot numbers.
description.state_variables: The system tracks four pieces of state: (1) For each acceptor, the highest ballot number it has participated in or promised to participate in. (2) For each acceptor, the ballot number of its most recent vote (negative one if no vote cast). (3) For each acceptor, the value of its most recent vote (a distinguished sentinel if no vote cast). (4) The set of all messages ever sent in the system. Messages are accumulated and never removed.
description.initial_state: All acceptor participation thresholds are negative one. All acceptor vote-ballot trackers are negative one. All acceptor vote-value trackers are the sentinel value. The message set is empty.
description.actions: The protocol has four message-driven actions: (1) Phase 1a (Prepare): A leader broadcasts a prepare message for its ballot number to begin a new ballot. No precondition prevents resending. (2) Phase 1b (Promise): An acceptor receiving a prepare message with a ballot number higher than its current threshold updates its threshold and replies with a promise message containing its most recent vote information (ballot number and value, or negative one and sentinel if it has not voted). (3) Phase 2a (Accept-request): Once a leader has collected promise replies from all acceptors in some quorum for its ballot, it selects a value and broadcasts an accept-request. If any responder reported a previous vote, the leader must choose the value associated with the highest reported ballot number. If none reported a previous vote, the leader may freely choose any value. At most one accept-request may be sent per ballot. (4) Phase 2b (Acceptance): An acceptor receiving an accept-request for a ballot at least as high as its current threshold updates its vote-ballot tracker, vote-value tracker, and participation threshold to reflect the new vote, and sends an acceptance message.
description.safety_properties: Consistency: at most one value is ever chosen. The specification maintains an inductive invariant with several components: type correctness, consistency between per-acceptor trackers and derived votes, constraints on message contents (promise messages reflect actual votes; accept-request messages are justified by quorum-based safety; acceptance messages correspond to prior accept-requests), and the invariant of the underlying voting specification. Two theorems are stated: the invariant is preserved by the specification, and the specification implements the voting specification.
description.liveness_properties: NOT_SPECIFIED
description.model_bounds: For model checking, three acceptors, two values, quorums as majority subsets, and a configurable maximum ballot number bounding the range. Two model configurations are provided: a tiny model with ballots zero through one, and a small model with ballots zero through two. Symmetry may be exploited over acceptor and value sets.
description.additional_assumptions: Any two quorums must overlap, though the correctness of the Paxos consensus algorithm's implementation of the voting specification does not itself depend on this assumption -- the voting specification is what becomes incorrect without it. A distinguished value not in the ballot set serves as the sentinel for acceptors with no previous vote. Messages are never removed from the message pool, modeling an asynchronous network where duplicate delivery is possible and message loss need not be modeled explicitly for safety properties. The specification defines a refinement mapping to the voting algorithm by deriving votes from acceptance messages, and proves implementation correctness through transitivity of refinement from Paxos through voting to consensus.

description.system_overview: This specification models a high-level voting-based consensus algorithm that is a direct abstraction of the Paxos consensus protocol, omitting message-passing details. Acceptors cast votes in numbered ballots, and a value is chosen when a quorum of acceptors have all voted for it in the same ballot. The specification was designed as a pedagogical formalization of the key ideas behind Paxos, as presented in a Turing Award lecture.
description.actors_and_components: The system has acceptors (processes that cast votes), values (candidates for consensus), and quorums (sets of acceptors satisfying an overlap property). For historical reasons, the voting processes are called acceptors. A quorum can be thought of as a majority subset of the acceptors.
description.state_variables: The system tracks two pieces of state per acceptor: (1) the set of votes cast by that acceptor, where each vote is a pair of a ballot number and a value; (2) a promise threshold indicating the minimum ballot number in which the acceptor will participate going forward.
description.initial_state: Initially, no acceptor has cast any votes (all vote sets are empty) and all promise thresholds are set to negative one (no promises made).
description.actions: Two actions are available: (1) An acceptor may raise its promise threshold to any higher ballot number, preventing it from voting in lower-numbered ballots. This action does not change any votes. (2) An acceptor may vote for a value in a ballot, provided: the ballot is not below its current threshold; it has not already voted in that ballot; no other acceptor has voted for a different value in that ballot; and there exists a quorum that demonstrates the value is safe at that ballot number. Voting also updates the acceptor's threshold to the ballot number. Safety at ballot b means that for every lower ballot c, there is a quorum in which every member either voted for that value in c or can never vote in c.
description.safety_properties: Consistency: the set of chosen values contains at most one value. This is ensured by three invariant components: (1) every vote is safe at its ballot number, (2) at most one value is voted for per ballot across all acceptors, and (3) type correctness of all variables.
description.liveness_properties: NOT_SPECIFIED
description.model_bounds: For model checking, three acceptors, two values, quorums as all majority subsets of the three acceptors, and ballot numbers bounded to a small finite range (for example, zero through two). Symmetry can be exploited over both the acceptor and value sets. Deadlock checking is disabled.
description.additional_assumptions: Any two quorums must share at least one acceptor. Ballot numbers are the natural numbers. The specification includes proof outlines for the invariance theorem and an implementation theorem showing that this voting algorithm implements the abstract consensus specification through a refinement mapping. The chosen set is defined as the set of values for which some ballot has a full quorum of votes. The specification uses a proof system backend for formal verification.

description.system_overview: This is a model-checking configuration module that verifies an inductive invariant of the Prisoners specification. It checks that the conjunction of the type-correctness invariant and the counting invariant is preserved by every step of the next-state relation, confirming these properties are inductive.
