(2) Terminate: an active node becomes inactive. (3) Receive message: a node receives a pending base message from some sender, becoming active. If the node has no parent, the sender becomes its parent; otherwise, an acknowledgment is sent back to the sender. (4) Receive acknowledgment: a node receives a pending acknowledgment, decrementing its active children count. (5) Detach or declare termination: when a node is inactive, has no active children, and has a parent, it either declares termination (if it is the initiator/root) or sends an acknowledgment to its parent and clears its parent pointer.
description.safety_properties: Termination detection is sound: the termination detected flag can only become true when the system is actually quiescent, meaning all nodes are inactive, no acknowledgments are pending, and no base messages are in transit between any pair of nodes.
description.liveness_properties: If the system reaches a quiescent state (all nodes inactive and no messages in transit), then termination is eventually detected.
description.model_bounds: The set of nodes and the maximum number of pending messages are declared as constants. A state constraint bounds the number of pending acknowledgments per node and the number of pending messages between any pair of nodes to keep the state space finite for model checking.
description.additional_assumptions: The set of nodes is finite. The initiator is a member of the node set. Weak fairness is assumed for each node process. The PlusCal algorithm is translated to TLA+ and the specification includes both the algorithmic description and the generated TLA+ translation.

description.system_overview: This specification models Dijkstra's algorithm for distributed termination detection on a ring, published as EWD 840: 'Derivation of a termination detection algorithm for distributed computations' by Dijkstra, Feijen, and van Gasteren (Information Processing Letters 16:217-219, 1983). The algorithm detects when all nodes in a ring have become inactive, using a token that circulates around the ring. Nodes and the token can be colored white or black to track whether messages have been sent against the direction of token flow.
description.actors_and_components: The system consists of N nodes arranged in a ring (numbered 0 through N-1) and a single token that circulates among them. Node 0 is the initiator that starts and evaluates token rounds. Each node can be active (computing) or passive, and each node has a color (white or black). The token also has a color and a position indicating which node currently holds it. The system is divided into two subsystems: the termination detection algorithm (System) that controls token passing, and the underlying computation (Environment) that models nodes sending messages and deactivating.
description.state_variables: The system tracks: (1) the activation status of each node (active or passive), (2) the color of each node (white or black), (3) the current position of the token (which node holds it), and (4) the color of the token (white or black).
description.initial_state: The token is initially black. The activation status of nodes, node colors, and token position may take any type-correct values. This models an arbitrary starting state where the token's black color ensures no false termination detection.
description.actions: The algorithm defines the following actions: (1) Initiate probe: when node 0 holds the token and either node 0 is black or the token is black, it sends a white token to node N-1 and paints itself white. (2) Pass token: a non-zero node holding the token passes it to the next lower-numbered node if the node is inactive, or if the node or token is black (which will cause an inconclusive round). The token is stained black if the node is black; the node is then painted white. (3) Send message: an active node activates another node (simulating message delivery). If the activated node has a higher number than the sender, the sender paints itself black (since the message goes against token flow direction). (4) Deactivate: any active node may become inactive at any time.
description.safety_properties: The main safety property (termination detection) states that if the token is at node 0, the token is white, node 0 is white, and node 0 is inactive, then every node in the ring is inactive. Dijkstra's inductive invariant ensures this: either all nodes after the token position are inactive, or some node between 0 and the token position is black, or the token is black.
description.liveness_properties: If all nodes become inactive (termination occurs), then termination is eventually detected (the token arrives at node 0 in a white state with node 0 white and inactive).
description.model_bounds: The number of nodes N is declared as a constant positive natural number. For model checking, N must be instantiated with a specific finite value.
description.additional_assumptions: Weak fairness is assumed for the System actions (token passing and probe initiation), ensuring the termination detection mechanism makes progress. No fairness is assumed for the Environment actions. The algorithm implements a higher-level specification of synchronous termination detection in a ring.

description.system_overview: This specification provides a high-level abstract model of the termination detection problem in a ring of nodes with synchronous communication. It serves as the top-level specification in a refinement hierarchy, where Dijkstra's EWD840 algorithm is shown to implement this abstract specification. The specification captures the essential requirements of termination detection without prescribing any particular detection mechanism.
description.actors_and_components: The system consists of N nodes arranged in a ring. Each node can be active or inactive. A global termination detection flag indicates whether termination has been detected. The specification abstracts away the details of how detection is performed, allowing nondeterministic detection whenever all nodes are inactive.
description.state_variables: The system tracks: (1) the activation status of each node (active or inactive), and (2) a boolean flag indicating whether termination has been detected.
description.initial_state: The activation status of nodes is unconstrained (each node may be active or inactive). The termination detection flag may initially be false, or it may be true if all nodes happen to start inactive (terminated).
description.actions: Three types of actions are defined: (1) Terminate: an active node becomes inactive. Termination detection may (but need not) be triggered simultaneously if all nodes are now inactive. (2) Wakeup: an active node activates another node (simulating message delivery). The termination detection flag is unchanged. (3) Detect termination: when all nodes are terminated, the detection flag can be set to true. This is a separate action with weak fairness to ensure eventual detection.
description.safety_properties: Stability: once termination is detected, all nodes remain permanently inactive (terminated). This ensures that termination detection is not falsely triggered while some computation is still possible.
description.liveness_properties: If all nodes become inactive (terminated), then termination is eventually detected.
description.model_bounds: The number of nodes N is declared as a constant positive natural number. For model checking, N must be instantiated with a specific finite value.
description.additional_assumptions: Weak fairness is assumed for the detect termination action, ensuring that if all nodes are permanently inactive, detection eventually occurs. No fairness is assumed for node termination or wakeup actions. Communication is synchronous in this abstract model.

description.system_overview: This specification provides an abstract model of the termination detection problem in a ring of nodes with asynchronous communication. Unlike the synchronous variant, this specification accounts for messages that may be in transit (pending) between nodes. It serves as a high-level specification in a refinement hierarchy: EWD998 (Safra's algorithm) refines this specification, which in turn can be related to the synchronous termination detection specification.
description.actors_and_components: The system consists of N nodes arranged in a ring. Each node can be active or inactive and may have pending messages waiting to be received. A global termination detection flag indicates whether termination has been detected. The specification abstracts away the mechanism of detection, allowing nondeterministic detection whenever the system is terminated.
description.state_variables: The system tracks: (1) the activation status of each node (active or inactive), (2) the number of pending messages at each node (messages in transit that have not yet been received), and (3) a boolean flag indicating whether termination has been detected.
description.initial_state: The activation status of nodes is unconstrained (each may be active or inactive). No messages are pending initially. The termination detection flag may be false, or true if all nodes happen to start inactive with no pending messages.
description.actions: Four types of actions are defined: (1) Terminate: an active node becomes inactive. Termination detection may be triggered simultaneously if the system is now fully terminated. (2) Send message: an active node sends a message to another node, incrementing the receiver's pending message count. (3) Receive message: a node with pending messages receives one, becoming active and decrementing its pending count. (4) Detect termination: when all nodes are inactive and no messages are pending anywhere, the detection flag can be set to true.
description.safety_properties: The safe property states that if termination has been detected, then the system is actually terminated (all nodes inactive and no pending messages). A quiescence property ensures that once terminated, the system remains terminated.
description.liveness_properties: If the system terminates (all nodes inactive and no pending messages), then termination is eventually detected.
description.model_bounds: The number of nodes N is declared as a constant positive natural number. A state constraint limits the number of pending messages per node to at most 3 for model checking.
description.additional_assumptions: Weak fairness is assumed for the detect termination action. An inductive invariant combining type correctness and safety is provided for verification with the Apalache model checker. A quiescence action invariant and trace invariant are provided for alternative verification approaches.

description.system_overview: This specification models Safra's algorithm for distributed termination detection on a ring, published as EWD 998: 'Shmuel Safra's version of termination detection'. The algorithm extends Dijkstra's EWD 840 to support asynchronous message delivery between nodes while still assuming reliable message channels and non-faulty nodes. Each node maintains a counter tracking the difference between sent and received messages, and the circulating token accumulates these counters to determine whether all messages have been delivered.
description.actors_and_components: The system consists of N nodes arranged in a ring (numbered 0 through N-1) and a circulating token. The system is divided into two subsystems: System (the termination detection algorithm controlling token passing and probe initiation) and Environment (the underlying computation with message sending, receiving, and node deactivation). The token carries a position, an accumulated message counter, and a color.
description.state_variables: The system tracks: (1) activation status of each node (active or inactive), (2) color of each node (white or black), (3) a counter for each node representing the difference between messages sent and received by that node, (4) the number of pending (in-transit) messages at each node, and (5) a token record containing its current position, accumulated counter value, and color.
description.initial_state: Node activation and colors may take any type-correct values. All per-node counters are initialized to zero. No messages are pending. The token may be at any node, has a counter of zero, and is colored black.
description.actions: The algorithm defines the following actions: (1) Initiate probe: when the token is at node 0 and the previous round was inconclusive (token is black, node 0 is black, or the accumulated counter plus node 0's counter is positive), node 0 sends a fresh white token with counter zero to node N-1, painting itself white. (2) Pass token: an inactive node holding the token passes it to the next lower-numbered node, adding its counter to the token's counter and staining the token black if the node is black, then painting itself white. (3) Send message: an active node increments its counter and nondeterministically places a pending message at another node. (4) Receive message: a node with pending messages decrements its counter, paints itself black, and becomes active. (5) Deactivate: an active node becomes inactive.
description.safety_properties: Termination detection is sound: when the token is at node 0, the token is white, the token's counter plus node 0's counter equals zero, node 0 is white, and node 0 is inactive, then all nodes are inactive and no messages are in flight. Safra's inductive invariant ensures this through five disjuncts involving the relationship between the token position, node counters, pending messages, node colors, and the token color.
description.liveness_properties: If the computation terminates (all nodes inactive and no messages in flight), then termination is eventually detected.
description.model_bounds: The number of nodes N is a constant positive natural number. A state constraint limits each node's counter to at most 3, each node's pending messages to at most 3, and the token's counter to at most 9.
description.additional_assumptions: Weak fairness is assumed for the System actions (token passing and probe initiation). Message channels are reliable (no message loss). Nodes do not fail. The specification refines the abstract AsyncTerminationDetection specification through a refinement mapping. The algorithm is correct for arbitrary ring sizes.

description.system_overview: This specification models Safra's termination detection algorithm (EWD998) with explicit message channel modeling. Unlike the base EWD998 specification that uses counters for pending messages, this variant models channels as sequences (inboxes) containing typed messages. Both payload messages and the token are represented as messages in node inboxes, providing a more concrete model that is closer to an implementation while remaining faithful to the abstract algorithm.
description.actors_and_components: The system consists of N nodes arranged in a ring, each with an inbox (message sequence). The inbox holds two types of messages: token messages (carrying a counter and color for the termination detection algorithm) and payload messages (representing computation messages). There is always exactly one token message across all inboxes. The system is divided into System (token management) and Environment (computation message sending, receiving, and node deactivation).
description.state_variables: The system tracks: (1) activation status of each node, (2) color of each node (white or black), (3) a counter for each node tracking messages sent minus messages received, and (4) an inbox for each node containing a sequence of typed messages (both token and payload messages).
description.initial_state: All per-node counters are zero. The token (a black token message with counter zero) may start in any single node's inbox. Node activation and colors may take any type-correct values.
description.actions: The algorithm defines the following actions: (1) Initiate probe: when a token message is in node 0's inbox and the previous round was inconclusive, node 0 consumes the token from its inbox and appends a fresh white token to node N-1's inbox, painting itself white. (2) Pass token: an inactive node with a token in its inbox consumes it and appends an updated token to the next node's inbox, adding its counter and propagating/setting the black color as needed, then paints itself white. (3) Send message: an active node increments its counter and appends a payload message to another node's inbox. (4) Receive message: a node with a payload message in its inbox consumes it, decrements its counter, paints itself black, and becomes active. (5) Deactivate: an active node becomes inactive.
description.safety_properties: The specification refines the base EWD998 specification through a refinement mapping that extracts the token position and counter from the inbox structure and counts pending payload messages. All safety properties of EWD998 are inherited through this refinement.
description.liveness_properties: Inherited from the base EWD998 specification through refinement.
description.model_bounds: A state constraint limits the number of payload messages per inbox to less than 3 and each node's counter to at most 3.
description.additional_assumptions: The type invariant ensures there is always exactly one token across all inboxes (singleton-type constraint). Messages within an inbox are unordered in the sense that any payload message can be consumed regardless of its position in the sequence. The specification requires the Utils module for helper operators.

description.system_overview: This specification refines the EWD998Chan termination detection algorithm by replacing natural number node identifiers with arbitrary identifiers (such as strings) organized into a ring. It also generalizes the initiator to be any chosen node rather than always node 0, adds vector clocks for distributed event ordering, and tracks the number of token passes after termination for worst-case complexity analysis. The specification demonstrates how to model vector clocks in TLA+ and how to decouple the algorithm from a specific node numbering scheme.
description.actors_and_components: The system consists of a finite set of nodes organized into a ring using a bijective ring function. One node is chosen as the initiator of token rounds. Each node has an inbox for receiving messages, a local vector clock, and the standard termination detection state (activation, color, counter). Payload messages carry a source identifier and a vector clock timestamp.
description.state_variables: The system tracks: (1) activation status of each node, (2) color of each node, (3) a counter for each node, (4) an inbox for each node containing typed messages (token and payload messages with vector clock timestamps), (5) a vector clock for each node mapping all nodes to clock values, and (6) a pass counter tracking the number of token passes since termination.
description.initial_state: All counters are zero. The initiator's vector clock starts with its own entry at 1, all other entries at zero; other nodes' clocks are all zeros. The token starts at a specific node position (chosen for worst-case analysis). All nodes start inactive with black color. The pass counter is initialized based on whether the system starts in a terminated state.
description.actions: The algorithm defines the following parameterized actions (parameterized by node identity): (1) Initiate probe: the initiator consumes a token from its inbox, merges vector clocks, and sends a fresh white token to its ring successor. (2) Pass token: a non-initiator inactive node consumes a token, merges vector clocks, and passes an updated token to its ring successor. Both token actions increment the pass counter. (3) Send message: an active node increments its counter and clock, then sends a payload message with its updated clock to another node. (4) Receive message: a node consumes a payload message, merges vector clocks, decrements its counter, paints itself black, and becomes active. (5) Deactivate: an active node becomes inactive, increments its clock, and resets the pass counter if the system just terminated.
description.safety_properties: The specification refines EWD998Chan (with a refinement mapping that translates identifiers back to natural numbers), inheriting all its safety properties. Additionally, a worst-case bound property states that termination is detected within at most three full token rounds after the system terminates.
description.liveness_properties: Inherited from the EWD998Chan specification through refinement.
description.model_bounds: A state constraint is inherited from EWD998Chan, limiting payload message counts and counters.
description.additional_assumptions: The node set is finite and non-empty. Nodes are organized into a simple cycle (ring). The initiator is deterministically chosen. The specification uses a ring successor function and provides operators for converting between node identifiers and natural numbers for the refinement mapping. Weak fairness is assumed for each node's system actions.

description.system_overview: This specification is a PlusCal representation of Safra's termination detection algorithm on a ring, as described in EWD 998. It uses bags (multisets) rather than sequences to model message channels, reflecting that message ordering is irrelevant to the algorithm's correctness. The PlusCal algorithm is automatically translated to TLA+ and is shown to refine the base EWD998 specification.
description.actors_and_components: The system consists of N nodes arranged in a ring, each running as an independent fair process. A shared network variable maps each node to a bag of messages. Messages are either token messages (carrying a counter and color) or payload messages. Node 0 is designated as the initiator.
description.state_variables: The system tracks: (1) a network mapping each node to a bag of messages in its channel, (2) per-node activation status (active or inactive), (3) per-node color (initially black), and (4) per-node counter tracking messages sent minus received.
description.initial_state: The network contains a single black token message with counter zero at the initiator's channel; all other channels are empty. Node activation status is unconstrained. All nodes start with black color and zero counters.
description.actions: Each node process nondeterministically chooses one of five operations in each iteration: (1) Send payload: an active node sends a payload message to another node and increments its counter. (2) Receive payload: a node removes a payload message from its channel, decrements its counter, becomes active, and paints itself black. (3) Terminate: a node becomes inactive. (4) Pass token: a non-initiator node with a token in its channel, when inactive, atomically removes the token and places an updated token (with accumulated counter and propagated color) at the next node. (5) Initiate token: the initiator, upon finding an inconclusive token in its channel, replaces it with a fresh white token sent to node N-1.
description.safety_properties: The specification refines the base EWD998 specification through a refinement mapping that extracts token position, counter, and color from the bag-based network, and computes pending message counts from the network state.
description.liveness_properties: NOT_SPECIFIED
description.model_bounds: A state constraint limits each node's counter to less than 3 to bound the state space.
description.additional_assumptions: Weak fairness is assumed for each node process. The specification uses the Bags and BagsExt modules for bag operations. The PlusCal-to-TLA+ translation is included in the module. Liveness is not checked because fairness for the system sub-actions cannot be easily defined in the PlusCal framework.

description.system_overview: This specification models an asynchronous Byzantine consensus protocol for reliable broadcast, based on the algorithm in Figure 3 of Bracha and Toueg's 1985 paper. The protocol allows a set of processes to reach agreement on a binary value despite the presence of Byzantine (arbitrarily faulty) processes. It uses a three-phase approach with ECHO and READY message rounds to ensure that correct processes can reliably agree.
description.actors_and_components: The system consists of N processes. Each process is either correct or Byzantine. Byzantine processes can behave arbitrarily, including sending spurious messages. The protocol tolerates up to T Byzantine faults out of N total processes, with the constraint that N must exceed 3T. Up to F processes may actually become faulty in a given execution, where F is at most T.
description.state_variables: The system tracks: the total number of ECHO messages sent by all processes, the total number of READY messages sent by all processes, the number of ECHO messages received by each individual process, the number of READY messages received by each individual process, the current number of Byzantine processes, and the control location of each process (which indicates whether it has proposed a value, sent an ECHO, sent a READY, accepted, or become Byzantine).
description.initial_state: Initially, no ECHO or READY messages have been sent. No process has received any messages. No process is Byzantine. Each process starts in one of two proposal states representing its initial proposed value (either 0 or 1). Two special initial configurations are also defined: one where all processes propose 0, and one where all processes propose 1.
description.actions: The protocol supports the following transitions: (1) A process that has not yet become faulty and is still in its initial proposal state may become Byzantine, incrementing the Byzantine count, up to the fault bound F. (2) A process may receive an ECHO or READY message, incrementing its received count for the corresponding message type. When receiving, messages from both correct senders and Byzantine senders may be included. (3) A process that proposed value 1 sends an ECHO message. A process that proposed value 0 may also send an ECHO if it has received enough ECHO messages (at least the floor of (N+T+2)/2) or enough READY messages (at least T+1). (4) A process that has already sent an ECHO and has received enough ECHO messages (at least (N+T+2)/2) or enough READY messages (at least T+1) sends a READY message. (5) A process that has sent a READY message and has received at least 2T+1 READY messages decides (accepts).
description.safety_properties: Unforgeability: if all processes initially propose 0, then no process ever accepts. Agreement: if any process accepts, then eventually all correct processes accept or are Byzantine.
description.liveness_properties: Correctness: if all processes initially propose 1, then eventually some process accepts. Agreement as a liveness property: if any process accepts at any point, then eventually every correct (non-Byzantine) process also accepts.
description.model_bounds: For model checking: N=4, T=1, F=1. The process set is 1 through N. Control locations are six distinct states representing the two proposal values, echo-sent, ready-sent, accepted, and Byzantine.
description.additional_assumptions: The model uses a message-counting abstraction rather than tracking individual messages, since all messages are of the same type. Weak fairness is assumed on the actions of correct processes (receiving, sending echo, sending ready, and deciding), ensuring progress when actions are continuously enabled. The specification requires N greater than 3T, T at least F, and F at least 0.

description.system_overview: This specification models a parameterized reliable broadcast protocol with Byzantine faults, based on the one-round asynchronous reliable broadcast algorithm from Srikanth and Toueg's 1987 paper (Figure 7). The protocol allows correct processes to reliably deliver a broadcast message even when up to T out of N processes are Byzantine. Instead of modeling a dedicated broadcaster, the protocol uses initial values at each process to represent whether the broadcaster's INIT message was received.
description.actors_and_components: The system consists of N processes divided into two groups: correct processes and faulty (Byzantine) processes. The partition into correct and faulty sets is chosen nondeterministically at initialization, with exactly N-F correct processes and F faulty processes (where F is at most T). Correct processes follow the protocol; Byzantine processes may send arbitrary ECHO messages. The protocol requires N greater than 3T.
description.state_variables: The system tracks: the set of correct processes, the set of faulty processes, the control location of each process (indicating whether it received an INIT message, has not received one, has sent an ECHO, or has accepted), the set of messages received by each process (pairs of sender identity and message type), and the set of messages sent by all correct processes.
description.initial_state: Initially, no messages have been sent and no messages have been received. The set of correct processes has cardinality N-F, and faulty processes are the complement. Each process starts in one of two states: one indicating it received the broadcaster's INIT message, the other indicating it did not. A restricted initial state is also defined where no correct process received the INIT message (all start in the non-broadcast state).
description.actions: The protocol defines the following transitions: (1) A correct process may receive a set of new messages, which is a subset of all sent messages by correct processes combined with all possible messages from Byzantine processes. (2) If a correct process received the INIT message (starts in the broadcast-received state), it immediately accepts and sends an ECHO message to all. (3) If a correct process that has not yet sent ECHO receives at least N-2T ECHO messages from distinct senders but fewer than N-T, it sends ECHO to all but does not yet accept. (4) If a correct process that has not yet sent ECHO receives at least N-T ECHO messages from distinct senders, it sends ECHO and immediately accepts. (5) If a correct process that has already sent ECHO receives at least N-T ECHO messages from distinct senders, it accepts.
description.safety_properties: Unforgeability: if no correct process broadcasts (all start without the INIT message), then no correct process ever accepts. Type safety: program counters, message sets, and process sets remain within their defined domains throughout execution.
description.liveness_properties: Correctness: if all correct processes received the INIT message (all start in the broadcast state), then eventually all correct processes accept. Relay: if any correct process accepts, then eventually all correct processes accept.
description.model_bounds: For model checking: N=4, T=1, F=1. A second configuration for checking the no-broadcast case uses N=10, T=3, F=2. Messages consist only of ECHO type paired with sender identities.
description.additional_assumptions: Weak fairness is assumed on the combined receive-and-act steps of correct processes, ensuring that if a correct process can forever receive messages from correct senders and act on them, it eventually does. The specification includes a variant without fairness for checking safety-only properties (unforgeability). The model requires N greater than 3T, T at least F, and F at least 0. The specification includes formal proof support for the unforgeability property.

description.system_overview: This specification models a parameterized reliable broadcast protocol by message diffusion with crash failures, based on the algorithm described in Figure 4 of Chandra and Toueg's 1996 paper on unreliable failure detectors. The protocol ensures that if a correct process broadcasts a message, all correct processes eventually accept it, and if no correct process broadcasts, no correct process accepts. Processes may crash but do not behave maliciously.
description.actors_and_components: The system consists of N processes. Some processes may crash during execution, up to a maximum of F crashes (where F is at most T, and N exceeds 2T). Crashed processes stop participating entirely. The protocol has no dedicated broadcaster; instead, the initial state of each process determines whether it has received an INIT message from an external source.
description.state_variables: The system tracks: the set of currently correct (non-crashed) processes, the count of crashed processes, the control location of each process (indicating whether it has not received an INIT, has received an INIT, has accepted and broadcast ECHO, or has crashed), the set of messages received by each process (pairs of sender and message type), and the set of messages sent by all correct processes.
description.initial_state: Initially, no process has crashed and all processes are correct. No messages have been sent and no messages have been received. Each process starts in one of two states: one indicating it received an INIT message (will broadcast), and one indicating it did not. A variant initial state is defined where no process receives the INIT message.
description.actions: The protocol defines the following transitions: (1) A correct process receives a subset of sent messages, updating its received set to include all messages in that subset. (2) If a correct process starts with the INIT-received state, it accepts and broadcasts an ECHO message to all processes. (3) If a correct process that started without the INIT message receives any ECHO message, it accepts and broadcasts an ECHO message to all. (4) A correct process may crash (if fewer than F have crashed so far), which removes it from the correct set and transitions it to the crashed state. Each step combines receiving messages with one of these actions.
description.safety_properties: Unforgeability: if no correct process broadcasts (all start without the INIT message), then no correct process ever accepts. Type safety: all state variables remain within their defined domains.
description.liveness_properties: Correctness: if all correct processes received the INIT message, then eventually some correct process accepts. Relay: if any correct process accepts, then eventually all correct processes accept. Reliable channels: if an ECHO message is sent by a correct process, then eventually every correct process receives it.
description.model_bounds: For model checking: N=4, T=1, F=1. The process set is 1 through N. Only ECHO messages are used in the protocol.
description.additional_assumptions: Weak fairness is assumed on the combined receive-and-act steps of correct processes, ensuring that enabled actions eventually occur. The model assumes clean crash failures (no Byzantine behavior). The specification requires N greater than 2T, T at least F, and F at least 0. A separate specification variant exists for checking unforgeability with the no-broadcast initial state.

description.system_overview: This specification models the BOSCO (Byzantine One-Step COnsensus) algorithm from Song and van Renesse's 2008 paper. BOSCO is a one-step Byzantine asynchronous consensus protocol that allows processes to decide in a single communication round under favorable conditions. When a one-step decision is not possible, processes fall back to an underlying consensus protocol. The algorithm tolerates up to T Byzantine faults among N processes, requiring N greater than 3T.
description.actors_and_components: The system consists of N processes. The last F processes (where F is at most T) are designated as faulty (Byzantine) and may send arbitrary messages, including voting for both values simultaneously. The remaining N-F processes are correct and follow the protocol. Byzantine processes are not modeled with explicit actions; their influence is captured through the message-receiving mechanism that allows correct processes to receive arbitrary messages attributed to faulty senders.
description.state_variables: The system tracks: the control location of each correct process (representing its current phase: initial proposal of 0 or 1, sent vote for 0 or 1, decided on 0 or 1, or deferred to underlying consensus with value 0 or 1), the set of messages sent by correct processes (pairs of sender and vote type), and the set of messages received by each correct process.
description.initial_state: Initially, no messages have been sent and no messages have been received. Each correct process starts with a proposed value, either 0 or 1, chosen nondeterministically.
description.actions: The protocol proceeds as follows: (1) Each process receives a set of messages that may include messages from both correct and Byzantine senders. (2) A process that proposed 0 broadcasts a vote for 0 and moves to the sent-0 state. Similarly, a process that proposed 1 broadcasts a vote for 1 and moves to the sent-1 state. (3) After sending, a process waits until it has received messages from at least N-T distinct senders. Then: (a) If it received more than (N+3T)/2 votes for value 0, it decides 0 in one step. (b) If it received more than (N+3T)/2 votes for value 1, it decides 1 in one step. (c) If it received more than (N-T)/2 votes for 0 and fewer than (N-T)/2 votes for 1, it defers to the underlying consensus with value 0 (and similarly with the values swapped). (d) If neither value has a clear majority (both have at least (N-T)/2 votes), the process defers to underlying consensus with its own originally proposed value. One-step decisions have priority over fallback to underlying consensus.
description.safety_properties: Lemma 3 (agreement on one-step decisions): if any correct process decides 0 in one step, no correct process decides 1 in one step, and vice versa. Lemma 4 (consistency between one-step and underlying): if any correct process decides 0 in one step, no correct process defers to underlying consensus with value 1, and vice versa. OneStep0: if all correct processes propose 0, then no correct process decides 1, defers with value 0, or defers with value 1. OneStep1: if all correct processes propose 1, then no correct process decides 0, defers with value 0, or defers with value 1.
description.liveness_properties: NOT_SPECIFIED
description.model_bounds: For model checking: N=4, T=1, F=1. The process set is 1 through N. Correct processes are 1 through N-F, and faulty processes are N-F+1 through N. Two auxiliary parameters are computed: more than (N+3T)/2 and more than (N-T)/2, using integer division with ceiling.
description.additional_assumptions: The specification does not include fairness conditions; it uses only the safety part of the temporal specification. The one-step decision thresholds have strict priority: a process checks the stronger one-step conditions before the weaker underlying-consensus conditions. If N is greater than 7T, the OneStep0 and OneStep1 properties hold; they do not hold otherwise. The model requires N greater than 3T, T at least F, and F at least 0.

description.system_overview: This specification models a consensus algorithm that can reach agreement in one communication step under favorable conditions, based on the algorithm in Figure 1 of Brasileiro et al.'s 2001 paper. The protocol operates in an asynchronous distributed system with crash failures. If enough processes propose the same value, consensus is achieved in a single round; otherwise, processes fall back to an underlying consensus protocol.
description.actors_and_components: The system consists of N processes that communicate by message passing. Processes may crash (up to F actual faults, bounded by T maximum tolerated faults). The protocol requires 3T less than N. Crashed processes stop sending and receiving messages but do not behave maliciously. Each process proposes a value from a finite set of possible values.
description.state_variables: The system tracks: the control location of each process (proposing, deciding, calling underlying consensus, crashed, or done), each process's current preferred value, each process's decision value (initially a special bottom value indicating no decision), the set of all broadcast messages (both proposal and decision messages), the set of messages received by each process. Messages carry a type (proposal or decision), a value, and a sender identifier.
description.initial_state: Initially, every process is in the proposing state and has a randomly chosen proposed value from the value set. No process has decided (all decision values are bottom). No messages have been sent and no messages have been received.
description.actions: The protocol operates as follows: (1) A process may crash if the number of non-crashed processes still exceeds the fault bound, transitioning to the crashed state. (2) A process may receive a message from the set of broadcast messages that it has not yet received. (3) In the propose phase, a process broadcasts a proposal message containing its preferred value and moves to the deciding phase. (4) In the deciding phase, once a process has received proposal messages from at least N-T distinct senders: (a) if all received proposals carry the same value, the process decides that value, broadcasts a decision message, and finishes; (b) if some value appears in at least N-2T of the received proposals, the process adopts that value as its new preferred value and falls back to the underlying consensus; (c) otherwise the process falls back to underlying consensus with its current preferred value unchanged. (5) If a process receives a decision message from any other process (regardless of its current phase, as long as it has not finished or crashed), it adopts that decision value, broadcasts a decision message, and finishes. (6) Processes that have finished or fallen back to underlying consensus may take a no-op step to avoid deadlock.
description.safety_properties: Validity: if a process decides a value, that value was proposed by some process. Agreement: no two processes decide different values. Additionally, if any process decided a value and another process falls back to underlying consensus, the fallback process's preferred value equals the decided value. Weak agreement: no two decided processes have different decision values (without the fallback constraint).
description.liveness_properties: Termination: eventually every process either crashes, finishes with a decision, or falls back to the underlying consensus protocol.
description.model_bounds: For model checking: N=4, T=1, F=1, with a value set of two distinct values and a special bottom value for undecided processes.
description.additional_assumptions: Weak fairness is assumed on receiving, proposing, the core decision logic, and processing decision messages from other processes. The specification requires 3T less than N, 0 at most F at most T, and N greater than 0. The protocol models only the one-step algorithm itself without the underlying consensus sub-protocol. Inductive strengthening invariants are included for verification support.

description.system_overview: This specification models a condition-based consensus protocol that uses the maximum proposed value to reach agreement, based on Figure 1 with condition C1 from Mostefaoui et al.'s 2003 paper. The protocol operates in an asynchronous system with crash faults and proceeds in two phases. If a sufficient condition on the input vector holds (enough processes propose the maximum value), the protocol can terminate; otherwise processes deterministically choose from all received values.
description.actors_and_components: The system consists of N processes that communicate by message passing. Processes may crash (up to F actual faults, bounded by T maximum tolerated faults), with the constraint that 2T is less than N. Crashed processes stop participating. Each process proposes an initial value from a totally ordered finite set of values.
description.state_variables: The system tracks: the control location of each process (broadcasting phase 1, waiting for phase 1, preparing, broadcasting phase 2, waiting for phase 2, done, crashed, or choosing), each process's local view of all other processes' values (an N-by-N matrix, initially filled with a special bottom value), each process's proposed value, each process's estimated value (computed as the maximum of its local view after phase 1), each process's decision value (initially bottom), the count of crashed processes, the set of all sent messages, and the set of messages received by each process. Messages carry a type (phase 1 or phase 2), a value, and a sender; phase 2 messages additionally carry an estimated value.
description.initial_state: Initially, each process is in the broadcast-phase-1 state. Each process has a proposed value drawn from the value set. All local views are filled with the bottom value. All estimated values and decision values are bottom. No processes have crashed. No messages have been sent and no messages have been received.
description.actions: The protocol operates in two phases: Phase 1: (1) Each process broadcasts a phase-1 message containing its proposed value and moves to the phase-1 waiting state. (2) A process may receive messages, updating its local view with the sender's value when the message type matches the current phase. (3) Once a process in phase-1 waiting has received phase-1 messages from at least N-T distinct senders, it computes its estimated value as the maximum value in its local view, then moves to broadcast phase 2. Phase 2: (4) Each process broadcasts a phase-2 message containing both its proposed value and its estimated value. (5) Once in phase-2 waiting, if a process receives phase-2 messages where at least N-T of them carry the same estimated value, it decides that value and finishes. (6) Alternatively, if a process has received phase-2 messages from all N senders without reaching the N-T threshold for any single estimated value, it moves to a choosing state. (7) In the choosing state, the process deterministically selects a value that appears in its local view and decides it. At any point, a process may crash if fewer than F have crashed so far.
description.safety_properties: Validity: if a process decides a value, that value was proposed by some process. Agreement: no two processes decide different values.
description.liveness_properties: Termination: eventually every process either crashes or finishes with a decision. Conditional termination (under Condition C1): if at least F+1 processes propose the maximum value among all proposals, the protocol terminates.
description.model_bounds: NOT_SPECIFIED
description.additional_assumptions: Weak fairness is assumed on receiving, broadcasting, phase transitions, and choosing. The specification requires 2T less than N, 0 at most F at most T, and N greater than 0. All values in the value set are distinct from the special bottom value. Condition C1 states that at least F+1 processes must propose the globally maximum value for guaranteed termination.

description.system_overview: This specification models a one-step consensus algorithm with zero degradation under crash faults, based on Algorithm 2 (lines 1-4) from Dobre and Suri's 2006 DSN paper. The protocol allows processes to reach consensus in one communication step when all processes propose the same value, with no performance degradation compared to standard consensus when proposals differ. Only the one-step algorithm is modeled, without the underlying consensus sub-protocol.
description.actors_and_components: The system consists of N processes, some of which may become faulty (crash). The protocol tolerates up to T faults, with up to F actually occurring (F at most T). The constraint N greater than 3T is required. Faulty processes may contribute messages with arbitrary values before or after crashing. Correct processes follow the protocol faithfully.
description.state_variables: The system tracks: the number of vote-for-0 messages sent by correct processes, the number of vote-for-1 messages sent by correct processes, the number of vote-for-0 messages attributed to faulty processes, the number of vote-for-1 messages attributed to faulty processes, the count of currently faulty processes, the control location of each process (initial proposal of 0 or 1, sent vote for 0 or 1, decided 0 or 1, deferred to underlying consensus with 0 or 1, or Byzantine/faulty), and the number of vote-for-0 and vote-for-1 messages received by each process.
description.initial_state: Initially, no messages of any kind have been sent (all message counts are zero). No process is faulty. Each process starts in one of two proposal states, nondeterministically choosing to propose 0 or 1. All received message counts are zero. Two special initial configurations are defined: one where all processes propose 0, and one where all processes propose 1.
description.actions: The protocol supports the following transitions: (1) A process that is not yet faulty may become faulty if the faulty count is below F. When becoming faulty, it may contribute a message for the opposite value. (2) A process that proposed 0 broadcasts a vote for 0 and moves to the sent-0 state. A process that proposed 1 broadcasts a vote for 1 and moves to the sent-1 state. (3) A process may receive a vote-for-0 or vote-for-1 message (if more have been sent than received, including messages from faulty processes). (4) After sending its vote, once a process has received at least N-T total messages, it decides based on the following rules: (a) if it received at least N-T votes for 0, it decides 0; (b) if it received at least N-T votes for 1, it decides 1; (c) if neither threshold is met and the process originally voted for 0, it defers to underlying consensus with value 0; (d) similarly if it voted for 1, it defers with value 1.
description.safety_properties: OneStep0: if all processes initially propose 0, then no process ever defers to underlying consensus with value 0, defers with value 1, or decides 1. OneStep1 (liveness form): if all processes initially propose 1, then eventually no process is in a state of having deferred with 0, deferred with 1, or decided 0.
description.liveness_properties: OneStep1 includes a liveness component: if all processes propose 1, eventually all processes reach a state where none has decided 0 or deferred to underlying consensus.
description.model_bounds: For model checking: N=4, T=1, F=1. The process set is 1 through N. Control locations include nine distinct states: two initial proposal states, two sent-vote states, two decided states, two deferred-to-underlying states, and one Byzantine/faulty state.
description.additional_assumptions: Weak fairness is assumed on receiving, proposing, and deciding actions for all processes, ensuring progress when these actions are continuously enabled. The model uses a message-counting abstraction rather than tracking individual messages. The specification requires N greater than 3T, T at least F, and F at least 0. When a process becomes faulty, it may inject a message for the value opposite to its proposal.
